title_en: Yimin Company v. Zhoukou Municipal Government of Henan Province, et al. — dispute over unlawful administrative act
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 58 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, if the specific administrative act under suit violates legal provisions and damages the reliance interests of the counterparty, but revoking such administrative act would cause significant harm to the public interest, the court shall confirm the illegality of the specific administrative act under suit and order the administrative organ to take appropriate remedial measures.
keywords_en: Administration; Illegal administrative act; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Henan Province; Legal person; State organ; Administrative Procedure Law; Illegality of the sued administrative act; Protection of reliance interests; Balancing of public interests; Partial support; Gas franchise operation right; Tendering and bidding; Administrative approval; Administrative litigation
full_text_en:
Yimin Company v. Zhoukou Municipal People's Government, et al.

— Administrative Action Illegality

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 58 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, where a specific administrative act under litigation violates legal provisions and impairs the reliance interest of the counterparty, but revocation of the administrative act would cause significant damage to the public interest, the specific administrative act under litigation shall be found illegal, and the defendant administrative organ shall be ordered to take appropriate remedial measures.

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Xing Zhong Zi No. 6

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Zhoukou Yimin Gas Co., Ltd. Address: Building 1, Nanshan Huojie, Zhoukou City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Ma Yiqing, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Weiping, Attorney at Beijing Jintai Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Zhoukou Municipal People's Government. Address: East Section of Qiyi Road, Zhoukou City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Gao Deling, Mayor of the City.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Shuyi, Professor at China University of Political Science and Law.

Agent ad litem: Ying Songnian, Professor at the National School of Administration.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Zhoukou Municipal Development and Planning Commission. Address: East Section of Qiyi Road, Zhoukou City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Yin Jianyong, Director of the Commission.

Agent ad litem: Ma Huaide, Professor at China University of Political Science and Law.

Agent ad litem: Xin Zhiting, Attorney at Henan Tuanjie Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Henan Yixing Industrial Group Co., Ltd. Address: No. 9, Huanghebei Street, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Li Shiqiang, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Song Yafang, Attorney at Henan Zhengda Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Zhigang, Attorney at Henan Zhongwang Law Firm.

Zhoukou Yimin Gas Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yimin Company) appealed to this Court against the administrative judgment (2003) Yu Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 1 of the Henan High People's Court in its case against the Zhoukou Municipal Development and Planning Commission (hereinafter referred to as the Municipal Planning Commission) for issuing the "Tender Plan for the Legal Person of the Zhoukou Natural Gas Urban Pipeline Network Project" and issuing the "Notice of Winning Bid" to Henan Yixing Industrial Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yixing Company), and against the Zhoukou Municipal People's Government (hereinafter referred to as the Municipal Government) for issuing the "Notice Concerning Henan Yixing Industrial Group Co., Ltd.'s Exclusive Operation of the Urban Pipeline Network Gas Project within the Planned Area of Zhoukou City." This Court formed a collegial panel with Zhou Honggeng as presiding judge, and acting judges Mao Baoping and Wang Zhenyu as members, and held a public hearing in this case on November 17, 2004. The appellant Yimin Company's legal representative Ma Yiqing and agent ad litem Zhu Weiping, the respondent Municipal Government's agent ad litem Zhang Shuyi, the respondent Municipal Planning Commission's agent ad litem Ma Huaide and Xin Zhiting, and the original third party Yixing Company's legal representative Li Shiqiang and agents ad litem Song Yafang and Zhang Zhigang appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The legal representative of the respondent Municipal Government, Gao Deling, and its agent ad litem Ying Songnian, and the legal representative of the respondent Municipal Planning Commission, Yin Jianyong, did not appear in court for reasons. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The facts found by the court of first instance were as follows: On April 26, 2003, the Municipal Planning Commission sent letters of invitation to bid to 13 enterprises, including Yixing Company and Yimin Company, to organize the tender for the legal person of the Zhoukou Natural Gas Urban Pipeline Network Project. On May 2, 2003, it issued the "Tender Plan for the Legal Person of the Zhoukou Natural Gas Urban Pipeline Network Project" (hereinafter referred to as the "Tender Plan"), which stated, "Entrusted by the Zhoukou Municipal People's Government, the Zhoukou Municipal Development and Planning Commission organized personnel to prepare the tender plan for the legal person of the Zhoukou Natural Gas Urban Pipeline Network Project." The plan stipulated that after the winning bidder was determined, the Municipal Government would entrust Zhoukou Construction Investment Company to participate in the project's operation (the Municipal Government revoked this company by Zhou Zheng [2003] No. 76 on August 15, 2003, and the company did not actually participate in the project's operation). The plan and its supplementary notices also stipulated that the bidder should "timely deposit RMB 50 million as a bid bond into the designated account in Zhoukou; the bid bond of the winning enterprise would be used for the construction of the Zhoukou natural gas project." After registering, Yimin Company did not participate in the final bidding activity because it failed to pay the RMB 50 million bid bond. On May 12, 2003, the bidding was formally held. During the bidding, the Municipal Planning Commission selected five experts from the expert database of Henan Fangyuan Tendering Agency Co., Ltd., and together with the Deputy Secretary-General of the Zhoukou Municipal Party Committee and the Deputy Secretary-General of the Municipal Government, a total of seven people formed the bid evaluation committee. On June 19, 2003, based on the bid evaluation results and investigation, the Municipal Planning Commission issued the "Notice of Winning Bid" to Yixing Company, which stated: "Henan Yixing Industrial Group Co., Ltd.: As the legal person of the Zhoukou Natural Gas Urban Pipeline Network Project, through invited bidding, recommended by the bid evaluation committee, and with approval from the Municipal Government, your company is determined to be the winning bidder." On June 20, 2003, the Municipal Government issued Zhou Zheng (2003) No. 54, the "Notice Concerning Henan Yixing Industrial Group Co., Ltd.'s Exclusive Operation of the Urban Pipeline Network Gas Project within the Planned Area of Zhoukou City" (hereinafter referred to as Document No. 54), which stated: "To promote the economic development of our city, improve urban infrastructure construction, and enhance residents' quality of life, the Municipal Government agrees to the opinion of the bid evaluation committee for the Zhoukou Gas Urban Pipeline Network Project, and Henan Yixing Industrial Group Co., Ltd. is hereby authorized to exclusively operate the urban natural gas pipeline network project within the planned area of Zhoukou City." After Document No. 54 was served, Yixing Company handled the relevant land use procedures for the natural gas pipeline network project, purchased pipeline facilities such as gas transmission pipelines, signed a "ship-or-pay" gas supply agreement with the West-East Gas Pipeline Branch of PetroChina Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as PetroChina Company) in November 2003, and began construction of the pipeline network project. Yimin Company believed that the above "Tender Plan," "Notice of Winning Bid," and Document No. 54 issued by the Municipal Planning Commission and the Municipal Government violated legal provisions and infringed upon its legally entitled right to operate pipeline gas, and thus filed an administrative lawsuit with the Henan High People's Court.

The court of first instance further found that: Yimin Company was registered with the industrial and commercial authorities in April 1999 (without having obtained a gas operation qualification), with a business scope including pipeline gas, gas appliances, high technology, and real estate. On July 7, 2000, the former Zhoukou Regional Construction Bureau, by Zhou Di Jian Cheng (2000) No. 10, issued a "Reply Approving Zhoukou Yimin Gas Co., Ltd. as the 'Pipeline Gas Exclusive Operator for Zhoukou City'" to Yimin Company. The main content of the reply was: "In accordance with the provisions of Ministry of Construction Order No. 62, Henan Provincial People's Government Order No. 47, Henan Provincial Construction Department Yu Jian Cheng (1996) No. 69, and the principle that 'only one pipeline gas operation unit may be approved in one city,' and based on the design plan and expert demonstration, this project can meet both the immediate industrial and residential demand for gas and connect with the West-East Gas Pipeline Project. Upon review, your company is approved as the pipeline gas exclusive operator for Zhoukou City." After obtaining this document, Yimin Company subsequently obtained the "Construction Land Planning Permit" for the gas station, and the "Construction Project Planning Permits" and "Construction Project Construction Permits" for laying gas pipeline networks on roads such as Daqing Road and Bayi Road in Zhoukou City (now Chuanhui District, Zhoukou City). By the time of the first instance judgment, Yimin Company had built a gas pressure regulating station in Chuanhui District, Zhoukou City, and had actually laid some gas pipelines on main streets and in some residential areas in the district. On September 20, 2002, facing the situation where two gas companies existed in Zhoukou City at that time—Yimin Company and Zhoukou Gas Co., Ltd. (jointly established by Zhoukou Municipal Government and Beijing Zhongran Company, later dissolved)—the executive meeting of the Municipal Government resolved: "Regardless of the circumstances, before the issue is clarified, Yimin Company's pipeline laying work must be halted. This matter shall be implemented by the Municipal Planning Administration Bureau." On September 23, 2002, the Zhoukou Municipal Planning Administration Bureau issued a notice, which stated: "In accordance with Article 33 of the 'Implementation Measures of Henan Province for the City Planning Law,' which provides that 'for the construction, expansion, or renovation of buildings, structures, roads, pipelines, and other engineering facilities within the urban planning area, the urban planning administrative department shall provide planning and design conditions, and the construction unit or individual must obtain a construction project planning permit,' and in accordance with the requirements of the executive meeting minutes of Zhoukou Municipal People's Government (2002) No. 5, regardless of the circumstances, before the issue is clarified, Yimin Company's pipeline laying work must be halted."

On November 9, 2003, the Zhoukou Municipal Construction Commission issued Zhou Jian Cheng (2003) No. 39, which revoked the document Zhou Di Jian Cheng (2000) No. 10 of the former Zhoukou Regional Construction Bureau on the grounds that granting Yimin Company the qualification as a pipeline gas exclusive operator lacked legal basis, did not comply with relevant regulations and normative documents, and constituted an ultra vires approval.

The Henan High People's Court held at first instance:

(I) Concerning the Plaintiff's standing of Yimin Company

In April 1999, Yimin Company had obtained a business license, and its business scope included gas. In July 2000, Yimin Company obtained a reply from the former Zhoukou Regional Construction Bureau regarding the grant of the pipeline gas exclusive operation right, which indicated that the gas project operated by Yimin Company could both meet the immediate industrial and residential gas demand of Zhoukou City (Chuanhui District) and connect with the West-East Gas Pipeline Project. From May to June 2003, based on the policy provisions of Ministry of Construction Jian Cheng [2002] No. 272, "Opinions on Accelerating the Marketization Process of Municipal Public Utilities" (hereinafter referred to as Ministry of Construction Document No. 272), regarding opening the public utility market and determining franchise operators through bidding, the Municipal Planning Commission and the Municipal Government conducted a tender for the natural gas pipeline network project in Zhoukou City and determined Yixing Company's exclusive operation right for the natural gas pipeline network project in Zhoukou City. Since Yimin Company's gas operation right had not been revoked or annulled at that time, Yixing Company's exclusive operation right for the natural gas pipeline network project directly conflicted with Yimin Company's gas operation right. If the administrative acts under litigation were established or produced legal effects, Yimin Company would be unable to exercise its natural gas operation right. Therefore, Yimin Company had a legal interest in the administrative acts under litigation and had standing as a plaintiff in this case.

(II) Concerning the legality review of the administrative acts under litigation

1. Legality of the Tender Plan

Yimin Company had obtained an industrial and commercial license for gas operations in 1999, and in 2000, the former Zhoukou Regional Construction Bureau, by Zhou Di Jian Cheng (2000) No. 10, approved Yimin Company as the pipeline gas exclusive operator. Under the new policy requiring the operation of public utilities to be opened and the operator to be determined through bidding, if a tender for the legal person of the Zhoukou natural gas urban pipeline network project was to be conducted, the issue of Yimin Company's pipeline gas operation right should have been dealt with first. The Municipal Planning Commission's issuance of the natural gas pipeline network project legal person plan while Yimin Company's gas operation right had not been revoked was procedurally unlawful.

The provision in the Tender Plan that the Municipal Government would entrust Zhoukou Construction Investment Co., Ltd. to participate in the operation of the Zhoukou natural gas pipeline network project, although its subjective motive was to strengthen the management of the public utility industry, did not comply with the national policy prohibiting the government from engaging in business activities. Therefore, the relevant content of the Tender Plan was improper. Regarding the plaintiff's allegation that the Municipal Government was taking a 35% "dry share" without investing any funds, due to insufficient evidence, this allegation was not sustained.

2. Legality of the Notice of Winning Bid

According to the State Council's regulations on the leadership system and competent authorities for the West-East Gas Pipeline Project, Article 2 of the General Office of Henan Provincial People's Government's Yu Zheng Ban (2002) No. 35, "Notice on Accelerating the Utilization Work of the West-East Gas Pipeline Project," and the division of powers among the functional departments of the Municipal Government, it could be determined that the Zhoukou Municipal Planning Commission had the authority to organize the tender.

The "Law of the People's Republic of China on Tendering and Bidding" (hereinafter referred to as the "Tendering and Bidding Law") did not prohibit the setting of bid bonds, and the Municipal Planning Commission's setting of a RMB 50 million bid bond was to ensure the winning bidder's operational capability and was not unlawful.

The Tender Plan stipulated that the tender would be conducted as open bidding, but in the actual tender, the Tender Plan was not publicly announced, and the procedure for invited bidding was applied. Moreover, the tender project in this case was a provincial-level key project. According to Article 13 of the "Measures of Henan Province for Implementing the Tendering and Bidding Law" and Article 2 of the Ministry of Construction Document No. 272, the open bidding procedure should have been applied. If the invited bidding procedure was to be applied, approval from the provincial people's government or the State Planning Commission should have been obtained. However, in this case, the use of the invited bidding procedure was not approved. Therefore, the Municipal Planning Commission's use of the invited bidding procedure without approval was unlawful.

According to Article 24 of the Tendering and Bidding Law, the preparation time for bidders shall not be less than 20 days. In this case, the defendant sent the invitation letters on April 26, notified the Tender Plan on May 2, and the bid opening was on May 12. The bidders' preparation time should be counted from the date they obtained the tender documents. From the date the defendant issued the Tender Plan to the bid opening, there were 10 days, which did not meet the legal requirement that the preparation time shall not be less than 20 days. Therefore, the preparation time given to the bidders by the Municipal Planning Commission was unlawful.

According to Article 37 of the Tendering and Bidding Law, experts should account for more than two-thirds of the members of the bid evaluation committee, and the others may be government representatives. In this case, the bid evaluation committee had seven members, of which five were drawn from the expert agency and had expert qualifications. The other two, the Deputy Secretary-General of the Municipal Party Committee and the Deputy Secretary-General of the Municipal Government, although not drawn from the statutory agency, were government representatives. Since the members with expert qualifications accounted for more than two-thirds of the bid evaluation committee, the composition of the bid evaluation committee in this case was not unlawful.

Article 7 of the Tendering and Bidding Law provides that tender activities shall be subject to supervision, but it does not specify that supervision must be conducted during the process. Therefore, the fact that the Zhoukou Municipal Planning Commission did not notify the administrative supervision department to participate during the organization of the tender was not unlawful.

In summary, the Notice of Winning Bid was unlawful in two respects: the application of the invited bidding procedure and the preparation time given to the bidders.

3. Legality of Document No. 54

Yimin Company obtained the gas operation right in 1999 and the exclusive gas operation right in 2000. Without Yimin Company's operation right and exclusive operation right having been revoked through legal procedures, the Municipal Government granted Yixing Company the natural gas pipeline network project operation right. Since natural gas is a type of gas, this practice created a conflict between Yimin Company and Yixing Company regarding the natural gas operation right. Although Yimin Company's exclusive operation right was revoked during the course of this lawsuit, at the time of the Municipal Planning Commission's tender and the Municipal Government's issuance of Document No. 54, Yimin Company's exclusive operation right had not yet been revoked, and its business license has not been revoked to date.

Document No. 54 was issued based on the tender. Since the Tender Plan and the Notice of Winning Bid were unlawful, Document No. 54 lacked a lawful basis and therefore constituted an unlawful administrative act.

Regarding Yixing Company's gas operation qualification and experience in gas operation, the State Council announced the abolition of the approval system for gas operation qualifications in the list of items subject to approval in 2002. Therefore, on this issue, Document No. 54's grant of the natural gas operation right to Yixing Company was not unlawful.

Regarding the existing pipelines and other facilities built by Yimin Company, the Municipal Government could take remedial measures to address them. Therefore, the Municipal Government's grant of the natural gas pipeline network operation right to Yixing Company did not necessarily mean that duplicate construction would result.

Based on the above review of the legality of the administrative acts under litigation, it could be determined that the Tender Plan, the Notice of Winning Bid, and Document No. 54 under litigation were unlawful. However, pursuant to Article 58 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as "Several Interpretations"), the three administrative acts under litigation should not be revoked, and the Municipal Government should take remedial measures to resolve the gas project constructed by the plaintiff Yimin Company. The specific reasons are:

1. Although the administrative acts under litigation had unlawful aspects, they did not fall within the circumstances where the winning bid result is naturally invalid under the Tendering and Bidding Law. Only invalid administrative acts are subject to revocation. Unlawful administrative acts are not necessarily invalid. In this case, although the administrative acts under litigation had some unlawful aspects, whether they caused the administrative acts to be invalid or subject to revocation should be determined in conjunction with other circumstances of the case.

2. Revocation of the administrative acts under litigation would have an adverse impact on the public interest of Zhoukou City. According to Article 58 of the "Several Interpretations," where an administrative act under litigation is unlawful but its revocation would cause significant damage to the national interest or public interest, the people's court shall render a judgment confirming the unlawfulness of the administrative act and order the defendant administrative organ to take appropriate remedial measures. In this case, revocation of the administrative acts under litigation would have the following consequences: First, it would affect the connection of the West-East Gas Pipeline Project in Zhoukou City and the use of natural gas by Zhoukou residents. According to Article 2 of the Ministry of Construction Document No. 272, which requires that operators of public utilities be determined through bidding, the pipeline gas operation right previously approved by the relevant administrative department of Zhoukou City for Yimin Company should be terminated, and new operators for the pipeline gas or natural gas pipeline network should be determined through bidding. The administrative acts under litigation in this case are actions to re-determine the natural gas pipeline network operator through bidding in accordance with the above Ministry of Construction Document No. 272. The most obvious unlawfulness is that the bidding was conducted and a new natural gas operator was determined without first dealing with Yimin Company's gas operation right procedurally. However, the problem is that the bidding under litigation has already occurred. If the administrative acts under litigation were revoked, the Municipal Government would, in accordance with procedural requirements, need to first handle Yimin Company's gas operation right and then re-organize bidding for the natural gas pipeline network project. Handling these issues would take a considerable amount of time. On the other hand, the issue of connecting the West-East Gas Pipeline Project in Zhoukou City is imminent. If the administrative acts were revoked, it would delay Zhoukou City's use of natural gas from the West-East Gas Pipeline and might even result in losing the opportunity to connect with the West-East Gas Pipeline Project in Zhoukou City. Second, Yixing Company signed a "ship-or-pay" gas supply agreement with PetroChina Company in November 2003 and will begin gas supply in July 2004. Revocation of the administrative acts under litigation would not only directly cause losses in gas purchase costs but also affect the timely use of natural gas by Zhoukou residents. Third, after the administrative acts under litigation were made, Yixing Company has made significant capital investments and signed a "ship-or-pay" agreement with PetroChina Company. If the administrative acts under litigation were revoked, Yixing Company, which was not at fault in the bidding process, would also suffer significant economic losses. Based on the above three points, it can be concluded that revocation of the administrative acts under litigation would cause relatively significant adverse impact on the public interest of Zhoukou City.

3. In light of the circumstances of this case, the natural gas project constructed by Yimin Company should be addressed by the Municipal Government through remedial measures. Although Yimin Company obtained its business license without having the qualification for gas operations—meaning its gas operation rights were illegal—nevertheless, the rights were approved by relevant administrative authorities, and Yimin Company had made certain capital investments and project construction based on the approval documents. The Municipal Government and relevant functional departments bear responsibility for this. According to Document No. 272 of the Ministry of Construction, which provides that public utilities shall be operated through franchising by bidding, Yimin Company's original gas operation rights should be abolished. At the same time, since the challenged administrative act is not revoked due to the need of public interest, and Yixing Company is responsible for operating the Zhoukou natural gas pipeline network, Yimin Company can no longer continue to operate pipeline gas or natural gas pipeline networks. Under these circumstances, the project construction and other asset investments made by Yimin Company based on the gas operation rights granted by the relevant administrative authorities will constitute losses for Yimin Company. The Municipal Government and relevant functional departments bear certain responsibility for this. Where Yimin Company's gas operation rights are terminated and its capital investments become losses, the Municipal Government should, in accordance with the principle of government good faith, take corresponding remedial measures to address the gas project constructed by Yimin Company.

(3) The claim for compensation raised by the plaintiff should be dismissed. The compensation claim raised by the plaintiff Yimin Company stemmed from the forced cessation of the gas pipeline project construction due to the challenged administrative act, resulting in direct losses such as employee wages, refunds to gas users, and inability to proceed with construction contracts normally. However, Yimin Company did not provide corresponding evidence during the court hearing. According to Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning Evidence in Administrative Litigation, which provides that the plaintiff should provide evidence before the court hearing, otherwise it shall be deemed as waiving the right to submit evidence. It should be determined that the plaintiff's submission of evidence exceeded the time limit. The corresponding losses claimed by the plaintiff are not supported by evidence, and the court does not uphold them. Regarding the claim for losses arising from breach of contract due to the inability to perform the RMB 500 million loan contract signed with Tianjin Donghai Gas Investment Company, since the contract had not yet entered into effect at the time, there should be no loss from non-performance. Regarding the claim for losses arising from breach of contract due to the inability to perform the RMB 500 million investment agreement signed with Henan March Wind Company, the agreement texts provided by the plaintiff during the court cross-examination were contradictory, and their authenticity could not be determined. Moreover, the agreement to establish a new company through a joint venture had not been implemented. Therefore, this loss claimed by the plaintiff is not supported. In summary, because the plaintiff failed to provide evidence and the losses could not be established, in accordance with Article 56 of the Several Interpretations, Yimin Company's compensation claim should be dismissed.

In summary, in accordance with Articles 58 and 56 of the Several Interpretations, and after deliberation by the trial committee of this court, the judgment is as follows: 1. It is confirmed that the Bidding Plan and the Notice of Winning the Bid issued by the Municipal Planning Commission, and Document Zhengzhou Zheng Wen (2003) No. 54 issued by the Municipal Government, are illegal. 2. The Municipal Government shall take corresponding remedial measures regarding the gas project constructed by Yimin Company. 3. Yimin Company's compensation claim is dismissed. Yimin Company, dissatisfied with the above administrative judgment of the Henan High People's Court, appealed to this court, arguing as follows: (1) The challenged specific administrative acts also have the following problems: 1. The Bidding Plan's requirement that the Municipal Government entrust Zhoukou Construction Investment Company to intervene in the operation of the Zhoukou natural gas pipeline network, that the Municipal Government hold a 35% non-contributing share, and that a RMB 50 million guarantee deposit be paid, is seriously illegal. 2. The documents used by the court of first instance to support the Municipal Planning Commission's authority to issue the Notice of Winning the Bid are not laws, regulations, or rules, and the documents do not grant the Planning Commission the power to organize bidding. 3. The composition of the bid evaluation committee was illegal. 4. Yixing Company does not have the qualification for gas monopoly operations, and Document No. 54's grant of natural gas operation rights to it is illegal. 5. Document No. 54 leads to duplicate construction, because the document does not mention any remedial measures, and the government has not issued any remedial measure decision. (2) The judgment of the first instance does not correspond to the plaintiff's claims. Because the first instance judgment found that the challenged administrative acts were illegal in multiple respects and should be revoked, but it applied a confirmation judgment, which seriously violates the judicial principle of "no trial without complaint." (3) The first instance judgment misunderstood the concept of public interest. 1. Document No. 272 of the Ministry of Construction is not a law, regulation, or rule. The court of first instance used this document to deny the substantive rights that Yimin Company lawfully obtained for pipeline gas operations, which lacks legitimacy. Yimin Company, as private capital entering the public utility sector, fully complies with national industrial policies and the requirements of a market economy. 2. The "ship-or-pay" gas supply agreement signed by Yixing Company and PetroChina was signed after the court of first instance trial, and should not have been considered by the first instance court. 3. The so-called investments and losses of Yixing Company were all caused by agreements it unilaterally signed after the trial of the court of first instance. The so-called "unilaterally expanded losses" should not be protected by law, let alone considered as public interest. Additionally, Yixing Company did not provide evidence on the actual amount of its investment in the project. (4) The challenged specific administrative acts are seriously illegal and should be revoked, and there is no circumstance justifying the application of a confirmation judgment. (5) The appellee should bear the various direct losses caused to Yimin Company by its illegal acts. Yimin Company requests that the court of second instance revoke the first instance judgment, revoke the three challenged specific administrative acts, and order the appellee to compensate it for other direct economic losses of RMB 35 million, excluding the investment in laying pipelines.

The appellee, the Municipal Government, responded as follows: (1) The facts found by the first instance judgment are clear and supported by evidence. 1. Yimin Company's registered capital was only RMB 600,000 before the litigation began, and it had almost no construction before 2002. 2. The approval document issued by the former Zhoukou Regional Construction Bureau granting Yimin Company monopoly operation status had no legal basis, was an invalid administrative act, and had been self-corrected by the Zhoukou Construction Committee. 3. The Construction Land Planning Permit for the gas station and the Construction Project Planning Permits and Construction Project Construction Permits for laying gas pipelines on Daping Road, Bayi Road, and other sections in Chuanhui District were not lawfully obtained. 4. Although Yimin Company built a gas pressure regulating station in Chuanhui District, Zhoukou, and actually laid gas pipelines on the main streets of Chuanhui District, these were all results of forced construction without permits or with incomplete permits, and there were no acceptance certificates. Moreover, most of the works were implemented after the Municipal Government decided to stop work. (2) The original judgment correctly applied laws and regulations. The Municipal Government requests that the court of second instance dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The appellee, the Municipal Planning Commission, responded that the facts found by the first instance judgment are clear, the evidence is sufficient, the result of the judgment is just, the dismissal of Yimin Company's compensation claim has legal basis, and the procedure is lawful. It requests that the court of second instance affirm the first instance judgment.

Yixing Company responded that although the challenged administrative acts are partially illegal due to defects, revoking them would cause significant losses to the public interest of Zhoukou City. The first instance judgment confirming the illegality of the challenged specific administrative acts without revoking them found the facts correctly and applied the law correctly. The RMB 35 million loss claimed by Yimin Company does not actually exist, and the first instance judgment's dismissal of its compensation claim was proper. Yixing Company requests that the court of second instance dismiss Yimin Company's appeal and affirm the original judgment.

This court confirms the above facts found by the court of first instance. Additionally, during the trial of this court, it was found that on April 24, 2003, the Municipal Government Office included the Zhoukou regional network part of the "West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission" project as a key municipal project. Previously, the Henan Provincial Government Office also included the "West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission" city pipeline network and various large and medium-sized utilization projects in provincial key project management.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the Bidding Plan for the Zhoukou Gas City Pipeline Network Project Legal Person and the Supplementary Notice issued by the Municipal Planning Commission; the Invitation Letter for Bidding for the Zhoukou Natural Gas City Pipeline Network Project Legal Person; the Evaluation Method for Bidding for the Zhoukou Natural Gas City Pipeline Network Project Legal Person; the Report on the Prequalification of Bidders for the Zhoukou Natural Gas City Pipeline Network Project Legal Person; the Investigation Report on China City Gas Construction Group Co., Ltd. and Henan Yixing Industry Group; the bid evaluation scoring sheets and bid opening records of the evaluation committee; the Notice of Winning the Bid issued by the Municipal Planning Commission; Document No. (2003) 54 of the Municipal Government and its correction documents; Zhouban (2003) No. 24, the Notice of the Zhoukou Municipal Government Office on Further Accelerating the Construction of Key Projects in the Whole City; Zhoushu Wen (2000) No. 37, the Notice of the Zhoukou Regional Administrative Office on Establishing the Leading Group for the Implementation of the West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission Project in Zhoukou Region; Zhou Zheng (2002) No. 28, the Notice of the Zhoukou Municipal Government on Adjusting the Leading Group for the Implementation of the West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission Project; Yuji Touzi (2001) No. 839, the Reply of the Henan Provincial Planning Commission on the Proposal of the Zhoukou City Gas Transmission and Distribution Pipeline Network Project; the industrial and commercial registration materials of Zhoukou Construction Investment Company; Yujian Zongji (2003) No. 88, the Letter of the Henan Provincial Department of Construction on the Review Opinions of the Feasibility Study Report of the Zhoukou Natural Gas Transmission and Distribution Project; Yimin Company's business license; Zhoudi Jiancheng (2000) No. 10, the Reply of the Zhoukou Regional Construction Bureau on Approving Zhoukou Yimin Gas Company as a "Pipeline Gas Monopoly Operator in Zhoukou City"; the Construction Land Planning Permit for the gas station constructed by Yimin Company, and the Construction Project Planning Permits, Construction Project Construction Permits, and City Road Excavation Permits for laying pipelines; the summary of the executive meeting of the Zhoukou Municipal Government on September 20, 2002, and the notice of the Zhoukou Municipal Planning Administration on September 23, 2002, requiring Yimin Company to stop work; Yimin Company's appeal and relevant documents for claims; the Municipal Government's response; the Municipal Planning Commission's response; Yixing Company's response; and the trial transcript, all on file as evidence.

This court holds that Yimin Company filed lawsuits against the Bidding Plan and the Notice of Winning the Bid issued by the Municipal Planning Commission, and Document No. (2003) 54 of the Municipal Government granting Yixing Company exclusive rights to operate city natural gas. The legality of each of the above acts shall be reviewed separately.

I. On the legality of the Bidding Plan.

(1) The Municipal Planning Commission has the authority to organize the bidding work for the city natural gas pipeline network project. The Zhoukou city natural gas pipeline network project is part of the utilization work of the "West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission" project. Before the bidding activities in this case began, from the central government to the Henan provincial level, this work had been assigned to planning commissions at all levels. According to the spirit of the special meeting of the State Council in 2000, which "required the National Development Planning Commission to take the lead in establishing a leading group for the West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission project, to coordinate upstream and downstream connections in the project, and to implement markets and related policies," and according to Article 2 of the Notice of the Henan Provincial People's Government Office on Accelerating the Utilization Work of the West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission (Yuzheng Ban (2002) No. 35, issued on May 27, 2002), which provides that "planning commissions at all levels are responsible units for the utilization work of the West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission, cooperating with the people's governments at the same level and higher-level governments in performing various tasks," the Municipal Planning Commission has the right to participate in the utilization work of the "West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission." The Zhoukou city natural gas pipeline network is both a municipal key project and a provincial key project. According to Zhou Bian (2002) No. 25, the Plan on the Functional Allocation, Internal Structure, and Personnel Establishment of the Zhoukou Development Planning Commission, issued by the Zhoukou Municipal Establishment Committee on March 18, 2002, which provides that the Municipal Planning Commission is "responsible for bidding and tendering work in the construction process of municipal key projects or key projects entrusted by the province," the Municipal Planning Commission has the authority to organize the bidding work for the city natural gas pipeline network project and to issue the Bidding Plan. Although Article 4 of the Ministry of Construction's Order No. 62 of 1997, the Measures for the Administration of City Gas, provides that "the competent administrative department of urban construction of the local people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for the administration of city gas within its administrative region," given that the State Council and the Henan provincial government had assigned the utilization work of the "West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission" to planning commissions at all levels, this provision cannot be applied to this case. The appellant Yimin Company's argument that the bidding for the city natural gas pipeline network project should be responsible by the construction department in charge of city gas, and that the Municipal Planning Commission had no authority to organize the bidding, cannot be sustained and is not supported by this court.

(2) On July 7, 2000, the former Zhoukou Regional Construction Bureau issued Zhou Di Jian Cheng (2000) No. 10, approving Yimin Company as a pipeline gas monopoly operator (Article 2 of the Henan Provincial Measures for the Implementation of Gas Management provides that gas includes natural gas), and stating that it could "interface with the West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission project." Accordingly, Yimin Company had obtained the exclusive gas operation rights. Before the bidding activities began, Zhou Di Jian Cheng (2000) No. 10 remained in effect, clearly constituting an obstacle to the issuance of the Bidding Plan, the Notice of Winning the Bid, and Document No. 54. Although the Municipal Planning Commission had the authority to organize the bidding work for the city natural gas pipeline network project, under the circumstances where Zhou Di Jian Cheng (2000) No. 10 had already granted Yimin Company exclusive gas operation rights, in accordance with due process, the Municipal Planning Commission should first have lawfully revised, abolished, or revoked that document, and provided reasonable compensation for Yimin Company's lawful investments made in reliance on the approval, before issuing the Bidding Plan. Therefore, the Municipal Planning Commission's disregard of the then-effective Zhou Di Jian Cheng (2000) No. 10 and its direct issuance of the Bidding Plan constituted a violation of legal procedures and also damaged Yimin Company's reliance interests. The appellee Municipal Planning Commission argued that "monopoly operation" in Zhou Di Jian Cheng (2000) No. 10 meant professional operation, not exclusive operation, and thus the document did not constitute an obstacle to bidding and franchising. This court holds that, according to the principle cited in that document—"only one pipeline gas operator may be approved in one city"—and other legal bases, "monopoly operation" in the document should be interpreted as exclusive operation. The Municipal Planning Commission's defense lacks legal basis and is not accepted by this court.

(3) According to Article 40 of the Measures for Bidding and Tendering in Engineering Construction Projects (jointly issued by the State Planning Commission and five other ministries), which provides that "if a bidder withdraws its bid, its bid security will be forfeited," it can be seen that the purpose of setting a bid security is to ensure that bidders have genuine intent to bid and to provide guarantee for the smooth progress of the bidding activity. In contrast, the content of the Bidding Plan—"to ensure the smooth progress of the open bidding and to guarantee that capable enterprises construct the Zhoukou natural gas city network project, each enterprise shall, after registration, deposit RMB 50 million into a designated account in Zhoukou on time" and "the security of the winning bidder shall be used for the construction of the Zhoukou natural gas project"—shows that the main purpose of setting this security was not only to guarantee the bidding activity itself, but to provide financial assurance for the smooth progress of the "West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission" utilization project. Therefore, this security is not the bid security stipulated in the Measures for Bidding and Tendering in Engineering Construction Projects, and should not be subject to the restriction of Article 37 of that Measure, which provides that "the bid security shall generally not exceed 2% of the total bid price, but the maximum shall not exceed RMB 800,000." According to Article 26 of the Bidding Law, which provides that "a bidder shall have the capacity to undertake the bidding project," when formulating the bidding plan, the Municipal Planning Commission may set reasonable conditions reflecting the bidder's capacity based on the actual circumstances of the project. Given that the estimated investment in the Zhoukou natural gas city pipeline network project exceeded RMB 100 million, requiring bidders to have corresponding financial capacity, the Municipal Planning Commission's requirement for bidders to pay a RMB 50 million security was reasonable and did not violate the intent of the law. The appellant Yimin Company's argument that the Bidding Plan's provision of a RMB 50 million security exceeded the statutory maximum limit and was intended to exclude Yimin Company from participating in the bidding cannot be sustained.

(4) The condition set in the Bidding Plan that "the Municipal Government shall entrust Zhoukou Construction Investment Co., Ltd. to intervene in the operation of the Zhoukou natural gas city pipeline network project, jointly form a cooperative company, and hold 35% of the shares in the company" granted Zhoukou Construction Investment Co., Ltd. a privilege to directly participate in the project without going through the bidding process, which violates the provision of Document No. 272 of the Ministry of Construction that "the construction of operational municipal public utilities such as water supply, gas supply, heat supply, sewage treatment, and garbage disposal shall select investment entities through open public bidding." However, this clause was not implemented, and the Municipal Government did not obtain any equity income under this clause. Therefore, the appellant Yimin Company's argument that the Municipal Government's taking of a 35% non-contributing share was seriously illegal and even constituted a crime lacks factual basis.

II. On the legality of the Notice of Winning the Bid.

(1) Since Zhou Di Jian Cheng (2000) No. 10 constituted a legal obstacle to the entire bidding activity, the Municipal Planning Commission, up to the time it issued the Notice of Winning the Bid to Yixing Company, still had not addressed Zhou Di Jian Cheng (2000) No. 10 to remove the legal obstacle. This constitutes a violation of legal procedures and damages Yimin Company's reliance interests.

(2) According to Article 13 of the Henan Province Measures for the Implementation of the Bidding Law, for key government projects, public bidding shall in principle be adopted. Invitation bidding may only be used if two conditions are met: first, the situation falls under one of the following: (1) the project is technically complex or has special requirements, and only a few potential bidders are available; (2) there are special requirements for the protection of proprietary technology and patent rights; (3) limited by natural resources or environmental conditions; (4) adopting open bidding is not economically feasible; (5) other circumstances where open bidding is not appropriate as provided by laws and regulations. Second, it must be verified by the provincial development planning commission and then reported to the provincial people's government for approval. The bidding project in this case is a provincial key project. The Municipal Planning Commission, without explaining whether the bidding activity fell under any of the above five circumstances and without completing the lawfully required approval procedures, directly adopted the invitation bidding method, which constitutes a violation of legal procedures. The appellee Municipal Government argues that the illegality of the Municipal Planning Commission's use of invitation bidding only lies in the failure to complete the statutory approval procedures, which reflects an incomplete understanding of the illegality.

(3) According to Article 24 of the Bidding Law, which provides that "for a project that must be subject to bidding by law, the shortest period from the date of issuance of the bidding documents to the deadline for submission of bid documents by bidders shall not be less than twenty days," bidders shall be given at least 20 days for preparation. The preparation time given to bidders by the Municipal Planning Commission started on May 2, 2003, and ended on May 12 of the same year, totaling 10 days, which is clearly less than the statutory preparation time, constituting a violation of legal procedures. The appellee Municipal Government argued that because the timing of the bidding was very close to the scheduled opening of the "West-to-East Natural Gas Transmission" in Zhoukou, the shorter preparation time was understandable. This court holds that although the appellee Municipal Government's defense has some reasonableness, it cannot change the illegality of the act.

(4) Appellant Yimin Company argued that among the seven members of the bid evaluation committee, the five experts recognized by the court of first instance were all government officials rather than genuine experts. Appellee Municipal Planning Commission argued that Henan Fangyuan Tendering Agency Co., Ltd. was a provincial-level tendering agency, and the certificate provided by the company stated that all five individuals were senior engineers in the specialty of "industrial and civil construction" and were listed in the expert database. Chinese law does not prohibit officials from serving as experts; in fact, it is common for officials to possess professional titles. This Court holds that the evidence provided by Appellee Municipal Planning Commission can prove that the five experts on the bid evaluation committee all complied with the provision of Article 37, Paragraph 3 of the Tendering and Bidding Law, which requires that experts "shall be determined by the tenderer from the expert rosters provided by the relevant departments of the State Council or the relevant departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, or from the list of experts in relevant specialties within the expert databases of tendering agencies." The grounds of appeal raised by the Appellant are insufficient to negate the probative force of the evidence provided by Appellee Municipal Planning Commission. Accordingly, the fact that five of the seven members of the bid evaluation committee had expert status complies with Article 37, Paragraph 2 of the Tendering and Bidding Law, which provides that "for projects that must be subject to tender according to law, the bid evaluation committee shall be composed of representatives of the tenderer and experts in technical, economic, and other fields, with the number of members being an odd number of five or more, and the number of experts in technical, economic, and other fields shall not be less than two-thirds of the total number of members."

III. Regarding the Legality of Document No. 54

(1) According to the provision of the Ministry of Construction's Document No. 272, which stipulates that industries such as urban gas supply that "directly concern public interests" shall be subject to franchising and that "investors and operators shall be selected through public tenders invited from the society," the Municipal Government has the authority to determine the operator of the urban pipeline network project based on the bidding result. However, before doing so, it must first process Document No. 10 (Zhou Di Jian Cheng [2000] No. 10) in accordance with the law in order to remove legal obstacles. Nevertheless, without taking any action with respect to Document No. 10, the Municipal Government directly issued Document No. 54, which granted the winning bidder Yixing Company the right to operate the urban natural gas pipeline network project. This action not only violated statutory procedures but also harmed the reliance interest of Yimin Company.

(2) According to the State Council's Document No. 24 (Guo Fa [2002] No. 24), "Decision on Cancelling the First Batch of Administrative Approval Items," issued on November 1, 2002, and its annex, "Catalogue of the First Batch of Administrative Approval Items Decided to be Cancelled by the State Council," the qualification approval for gas enterprises has been abolished. This document had already taken effect before the commencement of the bidding activities. Therefore, Yixing Company's acquisition of the right to operate the natural gas pipeline network was not conditional upon obtaining the qualification for gas enterprise operations. The Appellant Yimin Company's claim that Yixing Company lacked the qualifications for gas operations and that Document No. 54's grant of natural gas operation rights was unlawful cannot be sustained.

(3) The Appellant Yimin Company argued that Document No. 54 granted Yixing Company an exclusive right to operate natural gas, which violated the provision of the Henan Provincial Planning Commission's Document No. 631 (Yu Ji Gui Hua [2002] No. 631), "Notice on Printing and Distributing the 'Henan Province West-to-East Gas Transmission Utilization Plan,'" which states that "existing gas sources and pipelines shall be utilized as much as possible on the basis of not changing their ownership and subordination relationships. Where conditions permit, dual gas source supply shall be implemented as far as possible." This Court holds that the provision cited by the Appellant Yimin Company is a guiding rule, not a mandatory rule. Issues such as whether existing gas sources and pipelines should continue to be utilized and whether dual gas source supply should be implemented fall within the scope of discretion of the Municipal Government and relevant administrative organs. Therefore, the Appellant Yimin Company's claim that Document No. 54 should be invalidated on the ground that it violates the relevant provisions of the Provincial Planning Commission's Document No. 631 cannot be sustained.

In summary, this Court holds that although the actions of the Municipal Planning Commission in preparing the "Tender Plan" and issuing the "Letter of Acceptance," and the Municipal Government in issuing Document No. 54, involved misapplication of the law and violation of statutory procedures, and affected the Appellant Yimin Company's reliance interest, if these administrative actions were to be revoked by judgment, the public interest would suffer the following harms: First, the bidding activities would have to restart, which would inevitably delay the progress of the "West-to-East Gas Transmission" utilization work in Zhoukou City. Second, because there may be more than one bidder with operational capability, the outcome of a new tender would be uncertain. If Yixing Company were not to win the bid, its legitimate investments made in reliance on the challenged administrative actions would turn into losses. Although such losses could be compensated by the government, they would ultimately be transformed into losses to the public interest. Third, if Yixing Company were not to win the bid, its "take-or-pay" contract signed with PetroChina Company Limited would also become void. The utilization of natural gas in Zhoukou City would require the new winning bidder to renegotiate with PetroChina, and the success of such negotiations would be uncertain. Under these circumstances, the citizens and enterprises of Zhoukou City would not only be unable to use natural gas in a timely manner but might even lose the opportunity to connect to the "West-to-East Gas Transmission" project in Zhoukou, thereby adversely affecting the economic development and social life of Zhoukou City. According to the provision of Article 58 of the "Several Interpretations" (of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law), which states that "if the specific administrative act under suit is illegal, but its revocation will cause major harm to the national interest or the public interest, the people's court shall render a judgment confirming the illegality of the specific administrative act under suit and order the defendant administrative organ to take corresponding remedial measures," the judgment shall confirm the illegality of the specific administrative acts under suit and, at the same time, order the Appellee Municipal Government and Municipal Planning Commission to take corresponding remedial measures. Since Document No. 10 (Zhou Di Jian Cheng [2000] No. 10) has been revoked by the Zhoukou City Construction Bureau, it no longer constitutes a legal obstacle to the challenged administrative acts. Therefore, in this case, remedial measures should focus on compensating for the loss of interests of Yimin Company in order to achieve a balance between the public interest and individual interests. The judgment of the court of first instance confirming the illegality of the specific administrative acts under suit was not improper, but its judgment on remedial measures had two deficiencies: First, in accordance with the spirit of the law, to prevent administrative organs from indefinitely delaying their obligation to take remedial measures, the court may specify a reasonable period of time when the law does not explicitly prescribe a time limit. However, the judgment of first instance did not specify a corresponding time limit. Second, the judgment of first instance only ordered the Municipal Government to take corresponding remedial measures but did not impose any obligation on the Municipal Planning Commission.

IV. Regarding the Issue of Administrative Compensation

This Court holds that the evidence submitted by Yimin Company to the court during the first instance, including the construction contract for the natural gas supply project signed with Tianjin Donghai Gas Investment Company and the joint venture agreement signed with Henan March Wind Company, cannot prove the existence of the alleged losses. The court of first instance correctly made its determination based on the evidence submitted at that time and dismissed Yimin Company's compensation claim. The evidence submitted by Yimin Company to this Court in the second instance, including the list of direct economic losses after June 2003, the audit report issued by Zhoukou Shenxin Accounting Firm on November 22, 2004, the construction contract between Yimin Company and the Southeast Branch of China Water Resources and Hydropower Minjiang Engineering Bureau and the latter's claim letter, the construction contract between Yimin Company and Henan Jianyuan Gas Engineering Company and the latter's detailed statement of project claims, the lease agreement between Yimin Company and Wang Xuetang for the lease of premises and factory buildings and the latter's payment demand notice, the construction contract between Yimin Company and Henan Xieli Engineering Construction Group and the latter's notice demanding payment for the project, and certificates from some gas users who had already been connected and those awaiting connection, was obtained after the judgment of first instance. Since Yimin Company was unable to submit this evidence to the court during the first instance, it is permissible to submit it to the court of second instance. However, this evidence cannot be used to support its administrative compensation claim of RMB 35 million for direct economic losses other than investments such as pipeline laying, which it sought from the Municipal Government and the Municipal Planning Commission. First, apart from the premises and factory building lease agreement, the evidence submitted all falls within the category of investments such as pipeline laying, which goes beyond the scope of the administrative compensation claim raised, and therefore this evidence is irrelevant to this case. Second, the losses from the expenses for leasing premises and factory buildings were caused by the work stoppage, which was a consequence of the work stoppage notice issued by the Zhoukou City Planning Bureau, and there is no causal relationship with the challenged specific administrative acts. Third, apart from the audit report, the evidence is proof of debts that have not yet been fulfilled, which have not yet been converted into direct losses and do not fall within the scope of compensable losses under the State Compensation Law. Accordingly, Yimin Company's claim for administrative compensation for direct economic losses other than investments such as pipeline laying cannot be sustained. Pursuant to Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's "Regulations on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Administrative Compensation Cases," which provides that "if the plaintiff's claim lacks factual basis or legal basis, the people's court shall render a judgment dismissing the plaintiff's claim," the claim for administrative compensation filed by Yimin Company shall be dismissed.

In conclusion, pursuant to Articles 61(1) and 61(2) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm Items 1 and 3 of the judgment of first instance;

2. Amend Item 2 of the judgment of first instance to read: "Order the People's Government of Zhoukou City and the Development and Planning Commission of Zhoukou City to take corresponding remedial measures within six months from the date this judgment takes effect, to make reasonable compensation for the legitimate investments of Zhoukou Yimin Gas Co., Ltd."

The fee for the second instance of this case is RMB 100, to be borne by the Appellant Zhoukou Yimin Gas Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
